citation: Vallega-Neu, D. (2019). Truth, Errancy, and Bodily Dispositions in Heidegger's Thought. In C. Hadjioannou (Ed.), Heidegger on Affect (Philosophers in Depth, pp. 205–226). Palgrave Macmillan. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-24639-6_9
thesis: Heidegger held from 1930 onward that there is no event of truth without errancy, but never asked how attunement (Stimmung/Befindlichkeit) relates to errancy or how bodily disposition mediates that relation. Vallega-Neu argues (1) grounding attunements (Grundstimmungen) are inseparable from a double concealment of mystery and errancy, so even the most disclosive attunement remains vulnerable to being led astray, and (2) this vulnerability can be understood only once the lived body (Leib, 'bodying forth') is given a constitutive role: attunement just is the temporal texture of bodily spacing. Her destabilizing conclusion is that the bodily/attunement entanglement dissolves any clean separation between truth-revealing (grounding) attunements that hold errancy at bay and non-grounding attunements vulnerable to distortion -- all attunement, including Heidegger's own, remains ineliminably vulnerable to errancy. Chapter authored by Daniela Vallega-Neu; Hadjioannou is the volume editor only. Engages Heidegger's boredom analysis (FCM) only in a single passing citation (GA 29/30:238) supporting the historicity-of-grounding-attunements claim; no engagement with FCM's tripartite structure.

sections.title: Stimmung/Befindlichkeit as the under-thematized guide of Heidegger's later thought; Grundstimmungen list (Angst, deep boredom, restraint, presentiment, wonder) with FCM citation (GA 29/30:238); the unasked question of attunement's relation to errancy; Stolorow (2014) credited; announces the three-part structure and the Stimmung/Befindlichkeit terminological split

Truth, Errancy, and Attunements -- reading of 'On the Essence of Truth' (propositional truth/correspondence, openness, freedom as letting-beings-be, Gestimmtheit vs. Erlebnis/Gefuehl); the double concealment of mystery and errancy; Contributions to Philosophy's complex grounding attunement (Erschrecken/Verhaltenheit/Scheu); machination vs. lived experience (Erlebnis) vs. genuine experience (Erfahrung); Besinnung's differentiation of errancy from distortion (Verkehrung); critical digression on Heidegger's National Socialism and the body/spirit hierarchy the truth/distortion split reinstates; transition to non-fundamental, thing-directed attunements (fear, curiosity, the 'boring') as bodily dispositions

Attunement and the Body -- Zollikon Seminars' Leib vs. Koerper; Befindlichkeit as the attunedness determining Dasein's relation to world/others/self; thrownness-projection-language (saying/Rede) unity; being-addressed (Angesprochensein); Leiben ('bodying forth') as a mode of Da-sein, necessary but not sufficient for relation to things; train-station example; Heidegger's claim that understanding of being outstrips bodying forth; Vallega-Neu's extension of attunement as the 'temporal texture' of bodily spacing

Bodying Forth and Truth -- 'Origin of the Work of Art' world/earth strife; bodies as beings that 'shelter' truth's double concealment via their earthly, self-secluding quality; GA 70 §108 'Da-sein and Humans' schema; her central critical move questioning Heidegger's own separation of attuning being from bodily being

Consequence for errancy/distortion: the boundary blurs; attunements always multiple, entangled with other humans, animals, spaces, weather, technology (cell phones, wireless devices); meditation/'clearing' can only let attunements be; closes by situating Heidegger's own errancies together with everybody else's

41 endnotes -- German textual apparatus (GA volume-and-page citations), Sallis on the 'leap' in 'On the Essence of Truth' §§5-6 (n.6), Heidegger's Nietzsche-lecture and Basic Questions citations on feeling/attunement and the body (n.9)
Heidegger (Zollikoner Seminare 1987), Merleau-Ponty (Phenomenology of Perception), Stolorow (2014), Vallega-Neu (2005, 2012, 2018), Wolin (1993)

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: named once as a Grundstimmung example alongside Angst/restraint/presentiment/wonder; cited once (GA 29/30:238) as textual support for the historicity-of-grounding-attunements claim; no engagement with FCM's tripartite structure, Leergelassenheit/Hingehaltenheit, Zeitvertreib, or Augenblick

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: not named; analogical only (P/anticipatory-application) -- 'something appears as...boring' cited as her own example of a non-fundamental, thing-directed attunement, structurally parallel to FCM's first form though never mapped as such by the author

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: not named; same passing example as being-bored-by, undifferentiated from the first form by the author (P/anticipatory-application)

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: not treated in psychological vocabulary; analogical only (P/anticipatory-application) via the grounding/non-grounding attunement distinction -- grounding attunements are rare, totalizing, epoch-disclosive; non-grounding attunements are occasioned, thing-directed, multiple; register mismatch (ontological-historical vs. nomothetic-individual) flagged

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: not treated as a boredom construct; thematic resonance only via errancy's 'driven around from one thing to the next' structure and the critique of Erlebnis as foreclosing genuine questioning of meaning

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: not treated for boredom specifically; general temporality-of-attunement/bodying thesis developed instead (attunements as the 'temporal texture' of bodily spacing; bodies as 'ecstatically spatializing and temporalizing')

readings.text: Stimmung -- which Heidegger treats interchangeably with Befindlichkeit in Being and Time -- has guided his thinking and writing especially since the 1930s, even where not his explicit topic.

Grounding attunements (Grundstimmungen -- Angst, deep boredom, restraint, presentiment, wonder) unsettle Dasein from concern with particular beings into an experience of the occurrence of being as such; since FCM, such attunements are historical, determining how being discloses in certain epochs of Western philosophy for a people.
Heidegger never posed the question of how attunements relate to errancy, despite maintaining from 'On the Essence of Truth' (1930) onward that there is no event of truth without errancy.

Answering that question requires attention to the lived body (Leib), since it is through the body that Dasein is concretely situated in relation to being and beings; Stolorow (2014) credited for showing Heidegger's own privileging of attunement implicitly places the body at the core of his thought.

A terminological differentiation not native to Heidegger's own usage is introduced: Befindlichkeit names attunement's bodily register ('disposition'), Stimmung its non-bodily/linguistic register ('attunement') -- a split later destabilized in §3.

Reading 'On the Essence of Truth': even paradigmatically 'rational' truth-assertions are grounded in an open comportment that is always already attuning and attuned -- attunement precedes and conditions rational judgment.

Freedom is 'letting beings be' -- not an activity of a subject but a way Da-sein ('there-being') occurs, granting the relatedness of beings as a whole to humans rather than being exercised by humans over beings.

In §5, Gestimmtheit (being-attuned) is differentiated from Erlebnis (lived experience) and Gefuehl (feeling): all historical human comportment toward beings as a whole is attuned, whether or not explicitly felt or grasped.

Truth's disclosure is constituted by a double concealment: the 'mystery' (an originary concealment older than any disclosedness of this or that being) and 'errancy' (Irre) -- non-truth is not truth's opposite but its condition.

In Contributions to Philosophy, Heidegger thinks a complex grounding attunement proper to the epoch of being's withdrawal (machination): shock (Erschrecken), restraint (Verhaltenheit), and diffidence (Scheu, a drawing-near to what remains most remote, the divine).

Errancy names the way historical human beings are driven from the mystery toward what is readily available, one thing to the next; it belongs to Da-sein's inner constitution and cannot be removed, though experiencing it as errancy opens the possibility of not being led further astray.

Errancy is illustrated phenomenologically: anxiety arising from nowhere drives us to localize its cause somewhere in the body (a suspected illness) -- a back-and-forth between abyssal being and a determinate, locatable threat.

The forgetting of the mystery produces 'the plight of the lack of plight' (die Not der Notlosigkeit): people feel close to life and no longer feel the need to question being; 'lived experience' (Erlebnis) is more dangerous than machination since it forecloses questioning altogether.

In Besinnung (1938), errancy is further differentiated from distortion (Verkehrung, 'being turned in the wrong direction'): errancy belongs to truth's own clearing and carries a certain dignity, while distortion computes causes (drives, inclinations, pleasures) and reduces all things to the merely present-at-hand; awareness of distortion's danger allows one to ward it off.

Vallega-Neu contests this differentiation on two fronts: politically, Heidegger's claim to ward off distortion through steadfastness in truth sits uneasily beside his National Socialism, including a 1933-era address to NS labor-service beneficiaries equating 'knowing' with 'being master of the situation into which we are placed'; philosophically, the differentiation reinstates a spirit-over-body hierarchy (distortion glossed via bodily drives/appetites, truth via the 'announced god'), continuous with a tradition denigrating the body.

Heidegger's own drives/pleasures/inclinations vocabulary (the register of 'distortion') is reframed as itself a kind of attunement -- non-fundamental, thing-directed attunement, exemplified by something appearing as frightening or boring -- better understood as bodily dispositions than segregated from the attunement-vocabulary.

In the Zollikon Seminars, Heidegger approaches the body (Leib, against Koerper, the objective body) through spatiality rather than attunement -- a juxtaposition Vallega-Neu finds puzzling given his emphasis on attunement elsewhere.

Befindlichkeit is 'the attunedness that attunes and determines Dasein' in its relation to world, other Dasein, and itself; founded in thrownness and belonging together with understanding (Verstehen), reconceived as the opening of possibilities of being rather than an explicit cognitive act.

The unity of thrownness and projection is determined by language as 'saying' (Sagen), Heidegger's late recasting of Being and Time's Rede; on this basis humans can be 'addressed' (Angesprochensein) by beings -- applied directly to attunement in conversation with Medard Boss: 'Being attuned and being related are one.'

The body, thought out of Da-sein, occurs as Leiben ('bodying forth'), a mode of being; the body is 'the necessary but not sufficient condition' for relation to things, and bodying forth extends beyond the corporeal limit of the skin to 'the horizon of being in which I dwell' -- illustrated by the train-station example.

Heidegger insists the understanding of being reaches further than bodying forth: 'no bodying forth occurs' in the mere horizon of the understanding of being as such; bodily orientation (front/behind, above/below, right/left) is itself derivative of being 'directed' by what addresses us out of the openness of world.

Vallega-Neu's own extension: if the body articulates the temporal spacing of our relation to what addresses us, attunements name 'the temporal texture' of that bodily spacing -- 'a dense pluriform connective tissue' through which we are bodily connected to beings; attuned bodying forth precedes conscious perception.

Drawing on 'The Origin of the Work of Art' and her own earlier monograph (2005), bodies are beings that, in their earthly, self-secluding quality, delimit and configure 'concrete sites' of Da-sein -- of the there-being of truth -- much as a work of art holds open the strife between world and earth.

Our 'attuned, ecstatically spatializing and temporalizing' bodies are constitutive of truth's own appearing and non-appearing, and shelter truth's double concealment via our bodily relation to death and to our tendency toward beings.

The one late passage gesturing toward the event's relation to human bodiliness: GA 70 §108 ('Da-sein and Humans,' 1941) -- a schema running Being, Appropriation, Voice (Stimme), Attunement (Stimmung), Demand of courage (Zumutung), Gathered mood (Gemuet), Indwelling (Instaendigkeit), Disposition (Befindlichkeit, glossed as 'bodily being,' distinguished from its Being and Time sense).

Central critical move: 'begins calling into question' the distinction this GA 70 schema draws -- between attuning being (Stimmung, prior to and beyond the human) and bodily being (Befindlichkeit) -- proposing instead to rethink attunement as the very texture of 'human' bodying itself.

This destabilizes the boundary of 'the body' itself: 'our'/'human' placed in scare quotes; the boundary between what attunes/addresses us and our own bodying cannot be clearly marked -- an 'anonymous quality' of embodiment credited to Merleau-Ponty and, in Heideggerian terms, to the earthly, self-secluding character of bodies; Nietzsche credited with identifying this as unconscious drives/affects constitutive of the 'I.'

The blurred bodying/attunement boundary dissolves the errancy/distortion distinction of §1: attunements are 'always multiple and highly complex,' woven from other humans, animals, configured spaces, air, weather, light, machines, and the invisible traffic of cell-phone/wireless communication permeating bodily spaces.

Concentration or meditation can create a 'spacing' with respect to attunements (related to Heidegger's 'clearing'), but this spacing only lets attunements be; it cannot control which attunements become revelatory, and even in moments of clearing we remain blind to most attunements disposing our actions and thoughts.

Closing sentence generalizes this ineliminable blindness to Heidegger himself: 'Heidegger's errancies together with everybody else's' -- refusing to exempt Heidegger's political failure from the analysis or to treat it as its sole or sufficient explanation.

concepts.gloss: attunement / being-attuned; distinguished from Erlebnis (lived experience) and Gefuehl (feeling) in 'On the Essence of Truth' §5
disposition -- Vallega-Neu's translation for attunement's bodily register, glossed as 'how we find ourselves to be'; the attunedness that determines Dasein's relation to world/others/self
grounding/fundamental attunement (Angst, deep boredom, restraint, presentiment, wonder); historically epoch-determining, distinguished from non-grounding, thing-directed attunements (fear, curiosity)
lived experience (subjective-life incorporation, forecloses questioning) vs. genuine experience; Erlebnis judged more dangerous than machination
the ineliminable driving of historical human beings from the mystery of being toward readily available beings; belongs to Da-sein's inner constitution
'being turned in the wrong direction'; a further degeneration of errancy (Besinnung) that computes causes for everything and reduces beings to the merely present-at-hand
truth's own constitutive non-truth; the mystery is an originary concealment 'older than any disclosedness'; errancy is the second, differently-structured concealment
the lived body as a mode of Da-sein (bodying forth) vs. the objective/corporeal body; necessary but not sufficient condition for relation to things
hyphenated form emphasizing the being of the openness (not primarily human being) that also determines historical human being together with beings as a whole
being-addressed by things or by the claim of being; the basis on which Heidegger relates attunement directly to being-related in the Zollikon Seminars
the current epoch's determination of being as calculable and useable ('making'); judged less dangerous than lived experience because it does not fully foreclose questioning
'the plight of the lack of plight' -- the entrenched forgottenness of the mystery of being such that people no longer feel a need to question being at all

interlocutors.name: Martin Heidegger
interlocutors.role: primary text under analysis -- 'On the Essence of Truth' (GA 9), Contributions to Philosophy (GA 65), Besinnung (GA 66), the Zollikon Seminars (1987), 'The Origin of the Work of Art' (GA 5), Ueber den Anfang (GA 70), and the Nietzsche lectures (GA 43, 45)

interlocutors.name: Robert D. Stolorow
interlocutors.role: cited approvingly (2014, 'Heidegger, Mood and the Lived Body') for the claim that Heidegger's own privileging of attunement implicitly places the body at the core of his thinking

interlocutors.name: Maurice Merleau-Ponty
interlocutors.role: 'flesh' parallel to bodily texture; source of the 'anonymous quality' of embodiment Vallega-Neu extends to Heidegger's bodying forth

interlocutors.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
interlocutors.role: machination and lived experience developed by Heidegger in relation to will to power; credited by Vallega-Neu with identifying unconscious drives and affects constitutive of the 'I'

interlocutors.name: John Sallis
interlocutors.role: footnote 6: reads the 'leap' between §§5-6 of 'On the Essence of Truth' as 'a monstruous decentering of the essence of truth'

interlocutors.name: Richard Wolin
interlocutors.role: The Heidegger Controversy (1993), source of the National-Socialist labor-service address quote used to interrogate Heidegger's notion of 'knowing' (Wissen) versus blind fundamentalism

interlocutors.name: Rene Descartes
interlocutors.role: contrastive citation on the causal, subject-object account of bodily passions (agitations of the body), rejected as missing the relational structure of Dasein and attunement

interlocutors.name: Medard Boss
interlocutors.role: editor and interlocutor of the Zollikon Seminars; conversations (July 1965, March 1966) on being-attuned as being-related and as being addressed by the claim of being

interlocutors.name: Daniela Vallega-Neu (self-citations)
interlocutors.role: cites her own earlier work (The Bodily Dimension in Thinking, 2005; 'Bodily Being and Indifference,' 2012; Heidegger's Poietic Writings, 2018) for the fuller elaboration of the body/earth relation and bodily indifference this chapter can only sketch

tensions.label: Grounding vs. non-grounding attunements
tensions.poles: Angst/deep boredom/restraint/presentiment/wonder as historically epoch-disclosive, totalizing Grundstimmungen vs. fear/curiosity/the 'boring' as non-fundamental, thing-directed attunements relating Dasein to particular beings

tensions.label: Errancy vs. distortion (Verkehrung)
tensions.poles: errancy as dignified, ineliminable, belonging to truth's own clearing vs. distortion as a further degeneration -- 'being turned in the wrong direction,' computing causes and reducing beings to the present-at-hand -- which Heidegger claims can be warded off through steadfastness in truth

tensions.label: Spirit/body hierarchy embedded in the truth/distortion split
tensions.poles: Vallega-Neu's critique that Heidegger's differentiation covertly reinstates a metaphysical dualism privileging spirit/the 'announced god' (truth) over bodily drives and appetites (distortion), continuous with a tradition denigrating the body

tensions.label: Attunement as prior to/separate from bodily being vs. attunement as the texture of bodying
tensions.poles: Heidegger's own GA 70 §108 schema, which distinguishes Stimmung (arising prior to and beyond the human) from Befindlichkeit (bodily disposition) vs. Vallega-Neu's proposed collapse of this distinction, rethinking attunement as itself the texture of 'human' bodying

tensions.label: Claimed vigilance vs. actual political failure
tensions.poles: Heidegger's claim that awareness of distortion's danger allows one to ward it off, sustained by steadfastness in the truth of beyng, vs. his own historical failure to do so (National Socialism) -- the essay's self-critical closing wager that no one, including Heidegger, secures this vigilance
